extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology; readers of an advanced algebraic topology textbook
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions, and conditions relating spectra to (co)homology theories, mapping telescopes, homotopy colimits/realizations, cofibrations, and homotopy groups with coefficients; includes propositions and criteria guaranteeing when constructions produce (co)homology theories or homotopy equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology axioms (reformulated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each functor hn satisfies the homotopy, wedge, and Mayer–Vietoris (exactness) axioms; the reformulated exactness axiom asserts just the exactness of hn(X/A)→hn(X)→hn(A) for CW pairs (X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reformulation isolates exactness for CW pairs; to recover long exact sequences one also specifies natural suspension isomorphisms hn(X) ≈ hn+1(ΣX) as part of the cohomology theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural suspension isomorphisms (cohomology)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cohomology theory must have natural suspension isomorphisms hn(X) ≈ hn+1(ΣX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension isomorphisms are required (together with the other axioms) to obtain the usual long exact sequences and the stability properties used throughout the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology axioms (analogous reformulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The axioms for a homology theory can be reformulated analogously so that the exactness axiom asserts exactness of hn(X/A)→hn(X)→hn(A) for CW pairs, and natural suspension isomorphisms hn(X) ≈ hn+1(ΣX) are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reformulation is valid by the same arguments as for cohomology and is used to check that various constructions (e.g., stable homotopy groups) satisfy the homology axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy, exactness and wedge axioms (for stable homotopy groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stable homotopy groups π^s_n(X) define a reduced homology theory: suspension gives isomorphisms π^s_n(X) ≈ π^s_{n+1}(ΣX); the homotopy axiom holds; exactness follows from exactness of unstable sequences together with connectivity after suspension; the wedge axiom follows by reducing to finitely many summands and compactness arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification uses connectivity/suspension arguments, reduction to finite wedges, and passage to direct limits over suspensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct limit axiom (stronger than wedge)
rubrics_metrics.description: A stronger axiom sometimes required: hi(X) = lim--→ hi(X_α), the direct limit over the finite subcomplexes X_α of X (the 'direct limit axiom').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The homology theory defined by a spectrum satisfies this axiom; conversely, if a homology theory satisfies this (rather than just wedge) axiom then it can be represented by a spectrum (Adams 1971).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectrum is a sequence of CW complexes K_n together with basepoint-preserving maps K_n → K_{n+1}. (Often one assumes the K_n are CW complexes and maps are basepoint-preserving.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes suspension spectra; suspension spectra arise when K_n = Σ^n X with structure maps the identity. Weak homotopy equivalences K_n→ΩK_{n+1} are typical in stable contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy groups of a spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy groups of a spectrum K are defined as π_i(K) = lim--→ π_{i+n}(K_n), the direct limit computed using the compositions π_{i+n}(K_n) → π_{i+n+1}(ΣK_n) → π_{i+n+1}(K_{n+1}) induced by the structure maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus π_i(K) can be viewed as 'stable homotopy groups' by definition; in the suspension spectrum case this recovers stable homotopy groups of the space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology theory from a spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: For a spectrum K, define h_i(X) = π_i(X ∧ K). Then the groups h_i(X) form a reduced homology theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When K is the Eilenberg–MacLane spectrum with K_n = K(G,n) this homology theory is ordinary homology: π_i(X ∧ K) ≈ H_i(X;G). Exactness, wedge, and suspension axioms are checked via properties of smash products and direct limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficients and shifting (examples with Eilenberg–MacLane spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K = K(G,n) (Eilenberg–MacLane space), then for low dimensions (below a connectivity bound) the stable homotopy groups of K(G,n) agree with unstable groups and shifting dimensions yields a homology theory whose coefficient groups below dimension n agree with ordinary homology with coefficients in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can make this precise by taking direct limits over K(G,n) as n→∞ to recover ordinary homology on finite-dimensional CW complexes; dimension restrictions can be removed by passing to limits or suitable spectra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure of naive cohomology-from-spectrum definition (wedge problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: The naive attempt to define cohomology from a spectrum by h^i(X) = lim--→ h^{n}(X, K_n) runs into problems with the wedge sum axiom because the direct limit of a product need not equal the product of the direct limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This causes no problem for finite wedges but breaks the wedge axiom for arbitrary CW complexes; a corrected construction replaces K by a mapping telescope-based K' to restore the axioms for general CW complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping telescope correction (construction of K')
rubrics_metrics.description: To fix the wedge-sum problem for cohomology, associate to a spectrum K an adjusted spectrum K' with K'_n = lim--→ Ω^i K_{n+i} (mapping telescope / CW approximation). Then h^n(X) = h(X, K') gives the desired cohomology theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mapping telescope construction (and taking CW approximations) produces a spectrum weakly equivalent to K but with better homotopy-colimit behavior; careful use of equivalences ensures spectrum structure maps and axioms hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and use of mapping telescopes
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sequence Z_1→Z_2→··· the natural map lim--→ Z_n → lim--→ Z_n (mapping telescope) is a weak homotopy equivalence; mapping telescopes are used to form K' and to relate stable/unstable groups via direct limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises and propositions justify deletion of initial terms and use of mapping telescopes; CW approximations may be needed to stay within the defined class of spectra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realization/homotopy colimit of a diagram of spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a diagram of spaces X (vertex spaces X_v and edge maps f_e : X_v → X_w), the realization (homotopy colimit) X̌ is formed by starting with the disjoint union of vertex spaces and filling in a mapping cylinder M_f for each map f, identifying ends with the appropriate vertex spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'realization' avoids pathological collapse of the naive amalgamation and has better homotopy-theoretic properties (e.g., mapping cylinders, mapping telescopes, joins arise as examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: map of realizations is homotopy equivalence (Prop 4G.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all component maps f_v making up a map of complexes of spaces f : X → Y are homotopy equivalences, then the induced map of realizations X̌ → Ŷ is a homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the mapping cylinders M(f_v) forming a complex of spaces and deformation retractions; the mapping-cylinder realization deformation retracts onto X̌ and Ŷ, giving the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: When realization equals original space (criterion for open covers, Prop 4G.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open cover U = {X_i} of a paracompact space X, the natural map p : X_U → X (from the realization of the cover complex) is a homotopy equivalence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction of a partition of unity subordinate to U gives a section X→X_U embedding X as a retract of X_U; fibers deformation retract to the section, yielding p as a deformation retraction. Corollary: if all finite nonempty intersections are contractible, X ≃ nerve(U).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cofibration definition and property (homotopy extension property)
rubrics_metrics.description: A cofibration is a map i : A → B satisfying the homotopy extension property; in particular, when i is an inclusion this is the homotopy extension property for the pair (A,B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4H.1: If i : A → B is a cofibration then i is injective and a homeomorphism onto its image. Mapping cylinder constructions convert arbitrary maps into cofibrations A ↪ M_f, and the cofiber B/A plays the expected role in homotopy cofiber sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushout/pullback duality and homotopy variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Pushout (amalgamation) is a quotient of a coproduct, while pullback is a subobject of a product; homotopy variants (realization/hocolim and dual ∇X/holim) are obtained by replacing quotients with mapping cylinders and pullbacks with path-space constructions respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homotopy versions (realization and the dual construction ∇X) to obtain constructions with better homotopy invariance (e.g., for inverse limits, Postnikov towers, and dual iterated constructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy groups with coefficients (µ_n and exact sequence, Prop 4H.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n>1 define µ_n(X;G) = [M(G,n), X] (homotopy classes of basepoint-preserving maps from a Moore space). There are natural short exact sequences 0 → Ext(G, π_{n+1}(X)) → µ_n(X;G) → Hom(G, π_n(X)) → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This parallels the universal coefficient theorem for cohomology but with variables reversed; proof uses a free resolution 0→R→F→G→0 realized by maps of wedges of spheres and the cofiber sequence producing M(G,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of π_n(X; Z_m) via Moore spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Define π_n(X; Z_m) = [M(Z_m,n-1), X] = µ_{n-1}(X; Z_m). This choice aligns indexing so π_n(S^n; Z_m) ≈ Z_m and matches geometric intuition about cycles 'mod m'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose M(Z_m,n-1) as S^{n-1} with an n-cell attached by degree-m map; this gives the interpretation of elements as homotopy-theoretic mod-m cycles and leads to Hurewicz-type results relating π_n(X; Z_m) and H_n(X; Z_m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology decomposition construction (criteria (1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: To build a CW complex X with prescribed homology groups G_n one inductively constructs X_n with H_i(X_n) ≈ G_i for i ≤ n and zero above, where (1) X_1 = M(G_1,1), (2) X_{n+1} is the mapping cone of a cellular map h_n : M(G_{n+1}, n) → X_n with induced map h_{n*}: H_n(M(G_{n+1}, n)) → H_n(X_n) trivial, and (3) X = ∪_n X_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all h_n are trivial the result is a wedge of Moore spaces. A homology decomposition of a simply-connected CW complex Y is a homotopy equivalence f: X→Y where X is constructed this way; Theorem 4H.3 asserts existence for every simply-connected CW complex.
